correctness.rationale: For each fixed quantifier rank q, truncating within-class red/blue counts and multiplicities of E-class types at q yields a complete q-round Duplicator invariant: fresh or matched classes admit fresh color-compatible witnesses. Once r>=2q the nongeneric types have exactly j<q red or blue points, with means lambda_{n,j}=m2^{-r} binom(r,j); the generic class count tends past q. Multinomial counts jointly yield independent Poissons at finite means and concentration above q at divergent means. Thus all sentence limits exist if every lambda_j has an extended limit. Conversely the FO sentence asserting an E-class with exactly j red points has probability 1-(1-p_j)^m; its limit exists iff lambda_j extended-converges. Ratios lambda_(j+1)/lambda_j -> infinity force at most one finite positive critical j. The critical red-minority and blue-minority categories are disjoint and independent in the Poisson limit. The example m=n,r=ceil(log2 n) has distinct limits 1 and 1/2 for lambda_0. Finite exact multinomial/EF examples corroborate normalization only.

value.rationale: A natural question in finite model theory is when iid unary expansions preserve convergence of deterministic reducts. This class gives an exact classification for every m_n,r_n growth regime, a countable critical hierarchy, a computable limiting sentence law, and a concrete counterexample where the reduct has zero-one law but the expansion lacks convergence; the precise answer can guide future general expansion theorems.

limitations: Fixed FO sentences with arbitrary but fixed quantifier rank; iid fair colors, equal deterministic E classes, m_n,r_n both diverge, no order.
Does not assert general random-expansion sufficiency or biased/unbalanced block result.
